paragraphs.text: For although he knew that God was just, which was revealed in his ordinary working and another in his secret counsel, yet he uttered his affection to God, because he was not able to understand the reason he punished him.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: You do not well apply your medicine to the disease.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He condemns their zeal, who did not have knowledge, nor regarded they to comfort him, but always granted on God's justice, as though it was not evidently seen in Job, unless they had undertaken the probation of it.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: Your fame will come to nothing.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Is not this a revealed sign of my affliction and that I do not complain without cause, seeing that I am thus tormented as though I should tear my own flesh, and put my life in danger?
paragraphs.label: e
paragraphs.anchor: take my flesh in my teeth

paragraphs.text: By which he declares that he is not a hypocrite as they charged him.
paragraphs.label: f
paragraphs.anchor: hypocrite shall not come before him

paragraphs.text: That is, cleared and not cut off for my sins, as you think.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: To prove that God punishes me for my sins.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: If I do not defend my cause, every man will condemn me.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He shows what these two things are.
paragraphs.label: k
paragraphs.anchor: Withdraw thine hand far from me

paragraphs.text: His pangs move him to reason with God, not denying that he had sinned: but he desired to understand what his great sins were that he deserved such rigor, in which he sinned by demanding a reason from God why he punished him.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: You punish me now for the sins that I committed in my youth.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: You make me your prisoner, and so press me that I cannot stir hand or foot.
